user.title: Sign in to Amazon

data.otp_code: 6-digit code (only if you left the key empty)

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Amazon again
reauth_confirm.description:
Amazon asked to confirm the sign-in for {account}. Fill in only what changed: with an authenticator key saved you can just press Submit; without one, type the current 6-digit code.

{detail}

data.password: New Amazon password (leave empty to keep)
data.otp_secret: New authenticator key (leave empty to keep)

error.need_code: Amazon asked for a code. Add your authenticator key, or type the current 6-digit code from your authenticator app, and submit again.
error.captcha: Amazon showed a picture puzzle (it does this when a sign-in looks unusual). Sign in to amazon.com once in a browser on your home network, wait an hour, then try again.
error.device: Amazon asked where to send a code by text or email. Set up an authenticator app in Amazon's 2-Step Verification settings, then try again with its key.
error.challenge: Amazon asked for an extra check the helper couldn't pass. Wait an hour, then try again.
error.auth: Amazon didn't sign in. If you're sure the email and password are right, Amazon may be blocking automated sign-ins; the message below says what Amazon reported.
error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach Amazon. Try again in a few minutes.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check Settings > System > Logs for amazon_order_sync.
error.no_helper: Couldn't reach the Amazon helper on Zima. Check it's running (docker ps) and the address is right.
error.not_paired: The Amazon helper is already paired with another setup. On Zima, delete /DATA/AppData/amazon-helper/data/token and try again.

abort.already_configured: This Amazon account is already set up.
abort.reauth_successful: Signed in again. Order checks have resumed.

refresh.name: Check Your Orders now
refresh.description: Reads your Your Orders page once (never more than once per 20 minutes) and updates the Amazon Orders list.
